Background

In the data folder, you will find data about shark incidents in California between 1950-2022. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

Load the libraries

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Load the data

Run the following code chunk to import the data. In this chunk, I am removing NA’s.

sharks <- 
  read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv", 
           na=c("NA", "N/A", "Unknown", "NOT COUNTED", "", " ")) %>% 
  clean_names()

Questions

  1. Are there any “hotspots” for shark incidents in California? Show the top five counties with the most incidents.
sharks %>% 
  count(county) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n)) %>% 
  slice_head(n=5)
## # A tibble: 5 × 2
##   county            n
##   <chr>         <int>
## 1 San Diego        25
## 2 Humboldt         20
## 3 San Mateo        19
## 4 Santa Barbara    19
## 5 Marin            16
  1. Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents per county.
sharks %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=county))+
  geom_bar(aes(fill=county))+
  coord_flip()+
  labs(title = "Incidents per County", y="incidents")

  1. Are there months of the year when incidents are more likely to occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by month. Which month has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=month, fill=county))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(title="Incidents by Month", y="incidents")

The tenth month has the highest number of incidents, which is October.

  1. Is there a time of day when most attacks occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by time of day. Which time of day has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  ggplot(mapping=aes(x=time, fill=county))+
  geom_bar()+
  coord_flip()+
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size=5.5))+
  labs(title="Incidents by Time of Day", y="incidents")

The most incidents occur at 11:00.

  1. How do the number and types of injuries compare by county? Make a table that shows the number of injury types by county. Which county has the highest number incidents? (hint: your table should be in wide format)
sharks_wide <- sharks %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  count(injury) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = injury,
              values_from = n) %>% 
  mutate(total_incidents=sum(minor, none, major, `major*`, `none*`, fatal, `minor*`, na.rm=T))

sharks_wide
## # A tibble: 22 × 9
## # Groups:   county [22]
##    county      minor  none major `minor*` `none*` fatal `major*` total_incidents

##  2 Humboldt        2     9     7        1       1    NA       NA              20
##  3 Island - C…     1     3    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA               4
##  4 Island - F…    NA    NA     7       NA      NA    NA       NA               7
##  5 Island - S…     2    NA     2       NA      NA     1       NA               5
##  6 Island - S…     1    NA    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA               1
##  7 Island - S…    NA    NA    NA       NA      NA    NA        1               1
##  8 Island - S…     1     1    NA       NA      NA    NA       NA               2
##  9 Island - S…    NA    NA     1       NA      NA    NA       NA               1
## 10 Los Angeles     6     2    NA       NA      NA     1        1              10
## # ℹ 12 more rows

San Diego has the highest number of incidents

  1. Use the table from #5 to make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by county.
sharks_wide %>% 
  group_by(county) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=county, y=total_incidents, fill=county))+
  geom_col()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 0.85))+
  labs(title="Number of Incidents by County")

  1. In the data, mode refers to a type of activity. Which activity is associated with the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  group_by(mode) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  arrange(desc(n))
## # A tibble: 8 × 2
## # Groups:   mode [8]
##   mode                    n
##   <chr>               <int>
## 1 Surfing / Boarding     85
## 2 Freediving             36
## 3 Kayaking / Canoeing    30
## 4 Swimming               22
## 5 Scuba Diving           20
## 6 Hookah Diving          10
## 7 Paddleboarding          7
## 8 Walking in shallow      1

Surfing/Boarding is associated with the most incidents.

  1. Make a plot that compares the number of incidents by activity.
sharks %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=mode, fill=injury))+
  geom_bar()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 0.85))+
  labs(title="# of Incidents by Mode", y="incidents")

  1. Which shark species is involved in the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>% 
  group_by(species) %>% 
  count() %>% 
  arrange(desc(n))
## # A tibble: 12 × 2
## # Groups:   species [12]

##  2 <NA>            14
##  3 Hammerhead       3
##  4 Blue             2
##  5 Killer Whale     2
##  6 Leopard          2
##  7 Salmon           2
##  8 Blue*            1
##  9 Mako             1
## 10 Sevengill        1
## 11 Thresher         1
## 12 blue             1

Great White sharks have the highest incident number.

  1. Are all incidents involving Great White’s fatal? Make a plot that shows the number and types of incidents for Great White’s only.
sharks %>% 
  filter(species=="White") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=injury, fill=county))+
  geom_bar()+
  labs(title = "Great White Incident Types", y="incidents")

No not all injuries are fatal, majority being none.
